origins.section: 6.1 A Field Holds Text, Bytes or a Message
6.2 Binary Data Goes In as Bytes
6.3.1 The Receiving Side Needs the Declaration Too
6.3 Sub-fields Are a Nested Message That Only a Declaring Packager Can Carry
6.4 A Follow-up Copies the Fields It Lists and Leaves the Original Alone

gates.says: all 5 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-field-55-read: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-field-55-read: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-field-55-read: 6.1 states that getString on bytes gives their hex form, ten characters for five bytes (output shows 9F3602014B for a 5-byte ISOBinaryField), so 12 bytes give 24 characters.
recorded.prompt:q-pin-from-web-form: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pin-from-web-form: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pin-from-web-form: 6.2 says set(int, String) converts only if the message's packager marks the field binary, a new ISOMsg has none (the channel attaches its own at send), the notYet case stores 16 characters and fails to pack (16/8), and behind a QMUX the pack fails on the channel thread so mux.request times out and returns null.
recorded.prompt:q-tier-in-62: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tier-in-62: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tier-in-62: Section 6.3.1 says the stock iso87ascii.xml declares 48, 60 to 63 and 120 to 127 as text (IFA_LLLCHAR), and that every dotted path into a field declared as text returns null without an error, so getString("62.3") returns null.
recorded.prompt:q-two-steps-48: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-two-steps-48: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-two-steps-48: 6.3 says setting a new ISOMsg(48) replaces the field as set does with any component, shown by 'after set(new ISOMsg(48)): 48.1=MOT 48.2=null', and the reference table says set(ISOComponent) replaces what was there.
recorded.prompt:q-clearing-pin: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-clearing-pin: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-clearing-pin: 6.4 runs exactly this case: after Arrays.fill on copy.getBytes(52), 'the original's is all zeros: true', because clone() shares the byte fields and writing into the array getBytes returns writes into both messages.

recorded.prompt:q-field-55-read:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-field-55-read:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-field-55-read:b: 6.1 says getString on bytes gives their hex form, not one character per byte, and the output shows 10 characters for 5 bytes.
recorded.prompt:q-field-55-read:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-field-55-read:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-field-55-read:c: The 6.1 output shows getString=9F3602014B for a binary field, and the page and reference table give null only for a nested message or an absent field.
recorded.prompt:q-field-55-read:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-field-55-read:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-field-55-read:d: The 6.1 output shows getString on an ISOBinaryField returning hex without throwing, and the reference table lists getString as giving bytes as hex.
recorded.prompt:q-pin-from-web-form:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pin-from-web-form:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pin-from-web-form:b: 6.2 shows the 16-character value fails to pack against the binary field (Binary data length not the same as the packager length (16/8)), so nothing reaches the host.
recorded.prompt:q-pin-from-web-form:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pin-from-web-form:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pin-from-web-form:c: 6.2 says set asks the message's own packager, a new ISOMsg has none, and the channel calls setPackager only in BaseChannel.send, so the field stays 16 characters.
recorded.prompt:q-pin-from-web-form:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pin-from-web-form:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pin-from-web-form:d: 6.2 says jPOS converts hex in one case only, when an attached packager declares the field binary, and the notYet example shows hex stored as 16 characters.
recorded.prompt:q-tier-in-62:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tier-in-62:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tier-in-62:a: Sections 6.3 and 6.3.1 say the sub-field layout lives in the packager, and with the stock packager getString("48.2") returns null, so jPOS does not split a field just because a path asks.
recorded.prompt:q-tier-in-62:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tier-in-62:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tier-in-62:b: Section 6.3 says the sub-field layout is in the packager, not the message, and section 6.3.1 says both ends of a link need the same declaration.
recorded.prompt:q-tier-in-62:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tier-in-62:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tier-in-62:d: Section 6.3.1 shows getString("48.2") returning INV-20931 from a received message that the acquirer packager unpacked, so dotted paths are not limited to sub-fields your own code set.
recorded.prompt:q-two-steps-48:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-two-steps-48:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-two-steps-48:b: 6.3 and the reference table say set(ISOComponent) replaces what was under that field number, and the output shows the new component's 48.1=MOT in place.
recorded.prompt:q-two-steps-48:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-two-steps-48:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-two-steps-48:c: 6.3's output after set(new ISOMsg(48)) shows 48.2=null, so the earlier sub-fields are not merged in, and the page says the fresh ISOMsg(48) erases the other's sub-fields.
recorded.prompt:q-two-steps-48:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-two-steps-48:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-two-steps-48:d: 6.3 says field 48 becomes an ISOMsg holding the sub-fields and a dotted path reaches inside it, and the output shows 48.2 gone after replacement, so sub-fields are not stored under their full paths.
recorded.prompt:q-clearing-pin:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-clearing-pin:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-clearing-pin:b: 6.4 shows copy.set(4, ...) leaves the original's field 4 at 000000030000, so the messages are not linked and only writes into the shared array reach the original.
recorded.prompt:q-clearing-pin:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-clearing-pin:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-clearing-pin:c: 6.4 says clone() gives the copy its own field map and nested messages but the text and byte fields are the same objects as in the original.
recorded.prompt:q-clearing-pin:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-clearing-pin:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-clearing-pin:d: 6.4 says writing into the array that getBytes returns writes into both messages, so getBytes does not return a fresh copy.
